question: A photoelectric cell is operating with a stopping potential of $-3 \text{ V}$. If the anode is maintained at a retarding potential of $-1 \text{ V}$ with respect to the cathode, what will happen to the current in the circuit?

options.A: The current will be zero because the potential is negative
options.B: The current will be zero because $-1 \text{ V}$ is less than $-3 \text{ V}$
options.C: Current will flow because the retarding potential is not sufficient to stop the most energetic electrons
options.D: The current will flow in the reverse direction
